setting: You all live in Toulouse, France, and you know each other from the Saturday morning parkrun, where you have run, walked, and chatted together for years.
openers: Send a photo of the morning's route
Ask who is marshalling next Saturday
Post a link to the results page
Suggest coffee at the café after the run
opener: Post a link to the results page

Julie.knows: You know Jean-Luc as an older parkrunner who explains his splits, Rose as a young regular who always beats you to the cake table, Guillaume as your partner, and Annick as the marshal who waves everyone round the course.
Julie.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when something about parkrun needs sharing.

Jean-Luc.knows: You know Julie and Guillaume as fellow regulars who sometimes share lifts, Rose as the young barista who remembers your coffee order, and Annick as the marshal who has been volunteering longer than you have been running.
Jean-Luc.texts: You message the group now and then, usually to comment on a result or the weather.
Jean-Luc.style: Almost no emoji and no abbreviations.

Rose.knows: You know Julie as the teacher who always looks out for the younger runners, Jean-Luc as the retired engineer who orders the same drink every week, Guillaume as Julie's partner who timed your first run, and Annick as the marshal who has a word for everyone.
Rose.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly in quick bursts around parkrun days.
Rose.style: Plenty of emoji and texting abbreviations.

Guillaume.knows: You know Julie as your partner and fellow parkrunner, Jean-Luc as the retired engineer who always has an opinion on the course, Rose as the young runner you coach informally, and Annick as the marshal who has organised the volunteers for years.
Guillaume.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to share a result or a joke about the course.

Annick.knows: You know Julie as the teacher who brings her class to cheer the finish, Jean-Luc as the engineer who helps you with the timing kit, Rose as the barista who always has a smile for you, and Guillaume as the maths teacher who checks the course with you.
Annick.texts: You message the group now and then, usually to thank someone or confirm who is marshalling.
Annick.style: A little emoji and light abbreviations.

private_lines.Julie: You teach a class of primary school children in Toulouse, and your evenings go to marking and lesson planning. You live with Guillaume, and most weekends you run, shop at the market, and see friends.
private_lines.Jean-Luc: You are a retired engineer living alone in an apartment in Toulouse. Your days go to walks along the Garonne, tending a few plants on the balcony, and reading, and you run parkrun most Saturdays.
private_lines.Rose: You work shifts as a barista at a café in central Toulouse, and you study part-time in the evenings. You live alone in a small flat and spend free time running, seeing friends, and going out in the city.
private_lines.Guillaume: You teach maths at a secondary school in Toulouse, and your days are taken up with lessons, marking, and corridor duty. You live with Julie, and on weekends you run, do odd jobs around the flat, and see family.
private_lines.Annick: You are retired and live alone in a flat in Toulouse. Your days are filled with volunteering as a parkrun marshal, shopping at the market, and seeing your grandchildren, and you walk to the start line most Saturdays.

text: [link: parkrun results, Sat 28 Nov]
Thank you. I see I went out too fast at the second kilometre again.
Lol you always say that 😭 but you still beat ur october time
Ur 2nd km is always fast 😂 well done tho
The wind on the return leg did not help.
Annick was on the bend by the bridge. Did anyone else see her send the 5k lot the wrong way round the cone
I did not send anyone the wrong way. I pointed. There is a difference.
Ok.
On shift till 9 💀 anyone want to do the christmas market sun after run?
Can't sat, Guillaume's cousin's thing. Sun maybe?
Sun works 👍
Home. My feet are dead 🥲 cake table is mine next week
Frost on the balcony this morning. The geraniums will not survive another week.
Saturday I am on the finish funnel with the barrier. Jean-Luc can you bring the spare tags? The bag is at mine
Yes. I will collect it Friday.
Rose the cake table is first come first served, I have seen you run for it
Ur not the boss of the cake table 😤
Also did I send anyone the wrong way on the 5k? Annick pls tell me I'm fine
You were fine. Guillaume was fine too. Everyone was fine except the cone.
Ok.
[photo: reindeer Christmas cards, 22 of them, one with a moustache]
Annick if the kids come to the finish Saturday again I need them back at the school by 10:15
The Garonne is high this evening. Someone has moved the bench again.
Cant sleep. Bought a tiny tree for the flat 🎄 it is already too big for the table
Tree is too big for the table is honestly the best news this week 😂 where is it going then
The geraniums did not survive. Frost again overnight.
Tree is on the floor now 🙃 it's fine. It's standing up again, 3 books holding it
Jean-Luc the tags bag is by my door. The blue one, not the white one.
Friday. Blue bag.
Marking the test on square roots. Half the class says the root of 16 is 4 and 8. Lunch.
Guillaume do we still have the reindeer stickers or did they go to yours
Yours. Second drawer by the kettle.
Guillaume you check the course Saturday morning? Last year the cone moved again by the bridge.
Yes, 8:00. The cone is fine now.
Thank you.
The Garonne is quiet tonight. The bench is back where it was.
Marking. 31 to go. Don't let the tree win Rose
Cant sleep again 🥲 tree is standing up with 3 books and a shoe holding it
